title: Twenty-three years of subscribers, and where the money went
lede: AOL reported a subscriber count in every annual filing from its first to its last. Read in a row, they draw one hill. The revenue line follows it with a lag, and the write-downs arrive in a single year.

blocks.title: AOL subscribers, 1992–2014
blocks.subtitle: Millions of subscribers to the AOL service. See the note for the changes of basis.
blocks.xLabel: Fiscal years to June 30 through 2000; December 31 from 2001

points.title: The disks work
points.text: 3.0 million subscribers in June 1995, from 903,000 a year earlier.[^1]

points.title: Flat rate
points.text: $19.95 unlimited from December 1996. 8.6 million members by June 1997 despite the busy signals.[^2]

points.title: The merger is announced
points.text: 19.4 million U.S. subscribers in June 2000, five months after the Time Warner deal.[^5]

points.title: The peak
points.text: 26.7 million on September 30, 2002 and 26.5 million at year-end.[^6]

points.title: Free for broadband
points.text: After the August 2006 change of strategy the count falls by 6.3 million in a year, to 13.2 million.[^10]

points.title: Spun off
points.text: 5.0 million when AOL leaves Time Warner in December 2009.[^12]

points.title: Last report
points.text: 2.2 million at the end of 2014, before the sale to Verizon.[^14]

blocks.source: America Online 10-Ks for fiscal 1996, 1997, 1998 and 2000[^1][^2][^3][^5]; AOL Time Warner and Time Warner 10-Ks for 2002 to 2008[^6][^7][^8][^9][^10][^11]; AOL Inc. 10-Ks for 2009, 2011 and 2014[^12][^13][^14].
blocks.note: The basis changes three times. 1992–1997 are worldwide subscribers at June 30 (the service was almost entirely American until 1996). 1998 is North America at June 30. 1999 and 2000 are U.S. subscribers at June 30. 2001 onward are U.S. subscribers at December 31. The 26.7 million peak fell between year-ends and is not a point on the line.

Fiscal 1998–2000 as restated in the fiscal 2000 10-K for later poolings, including Netscape[^5]. 2001–2002 AOL segment[^6]; 2003–2004 AOL segment[^9]. 2005–2009 from AOL Inc.’s first 10-K[^12]; 2010–2014 from its last[^14]. The three bases are not strictly comparable: Time Warner’s own 2005 figure for the AOL segment was $8,283M against $8,202.1M in AOL Inc.’s later accounts.

blocks.subtitle: $ millions. Subscriptions were 82% of revenue in 2005 and 24% in 2014 (derived).
blocks.source: AOL Inc. 10-Ks for 2009 and 2014[^12][^14]. For 2005–2009 “Advertising and other” is the **derived** sum of the advertising and other lines (for 2005: $1,337.8M + $109.4M). Shares are derived: $6,754.9M ÷ $8,202.1M = 82%; $606.5M ÷ $2,527.2M = 24%.
